draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Bekal Fort! This is the largest fort in Kerala, spread over 40 acres right next to the beach. From above it's shaped like a giant keyhole.
draft.hungryLine: Bekal Beach Park has a food court, which is your easiest bet for a bite near the fort.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The fort is a minute's walk. Look for the Mukhyaprana Hanuman Temple, the stepped water tank and the tunnel to the south inside.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Climb an observation tower and just take in the sweeping view of the Arabian Sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Lonely Planet once picked Bekal as one of its top ten travel destinations.

legends.title: Where the cannons stood
legends.body: The tall towers you can climb today once held huge cannons, a couple of centuries ago. Picture them pointed out over the Arabian Sea.

legends.title: A giant keyhole
legends.body: Bekal Fort is famous for its shape, which looks like a giant keyhole. It's the biggest fort anywhere in Kerala.

tips.title: Go between 8AM and 5:30PM.
tips.body: Those are the fort's opening hours, so plan around them.

tips.title: Dress modestly for the temple.
tips.body: The Mukhyaprana Hanuman Temple sits inside the fort, so cover up a little if you want to look in.

story.title: Shivappa Nayaka builds
story.body: Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi built Bekal Fort in 1650 AD. It spread over 40 acres beside the beach.

story.title: Cannons on the towers
story.body: The fort's tall observation towers carried huge cannons. They looked straight out over the Arabian Sea.

story.title: On the travel map
story.body: Lonely Planet named Bekal one of its top ten travel destinations. A beach park with a food court and amusement rides opened nearby.

story.title: Seaplanes, maybe
story.body: Kerala is reviewing a plan for seaplanes linking Bekal with Kollam Ashtamudi, Kumarakom, Punnamada and the Paravur backwaters.
